original.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.

original.description: The ACCESS (Accelerating Commercialisation and Competitiveness of the European Space Sector) programme helps companies develop innovative commercial products and services that strengthen European competitiveness in both space and non-space markets. It fosters a diverse and dynamic space ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of commercialisation reach all Participating States.Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is the element of ACCESS programme specifically designed to accelerate the transformation of innovative ideas into market-ready space-based services and applications that deliver measurable socio-economic impact.BASS offers to companies and academia derisking tools to mitigate technical and commercial risks, shortening the path from concept to market. With a strong user-driven focus, BASS creates the conditions for commercial success and positions space as a driver of innovation, competitiveness, and lasting value for society.To deliver these outcomes, BASS offers a comprehensive support package which includes zero-equity funding, tailored business and technical expertise, project management guidance, ESA branding, and access to commercialisation networks. This ecosystem connects companies with customers, investors, and partners, enabling them to overcome market barriers whilesecuring sustainable growth through private investment and demand-driven adoption.BASS support is tailored to every stage of developmentfrom assessing the viability of new space-based applications, to designing, implementing, and piloting space-based solutions and supporting their expansion into new markets.

original.description: Space can be the ideal environment to exploit a wide range of phenomena and physical processes that are not possible under the effects of gravity experienced on Earth, such as different fluid dynamics, material behaviour or cell biology. Besides microgravity, space offers extreme conditions, such as huge temperature differences and radiation, as well as an unobstructed vantage point for remote sensing or communication. All these characteristics can unlock benefits for commercial businesses on Earth in a wide range of sectors from energy to food and pharmaceuticals production. Now, access to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has become easier thanks to established space service providers operating onboard the International Space Station (ISS): ESA ISS Commercial Partners and other service providers offer unique services along with clear pricing policies, which cover the complete service chain from preparation, launch, operations onboard the ISS, to sample return. The 'Commercial Applications enabled by Space Environments (CASE)' Open Call for Proposals aims to support the development of commercial services that benefit from microgravity and space environments.

original.description: The present Standard Call for Proposals is part of the Generic Programme Lines (GPL) "Industrial Competitiveness" of the Programme of Advanced Research in Telecommunications Systems (ARTES 4.0), in particular its Component B: Industry-Initiated Activities. The specific objective of Preparatory Activities is to carry out activities (typically Phase 0/A/B1) that may be required for the Partnership Project to reach a sufficient maturity level to be formally proposed as an Industry-Initiated Partnership Project to be conducted in the framework of this Generic Programme Line or a Strategic Programme Line. Industry-Initiated Preparatory Activities of this Standard Call for Proposals shall be aimed at supporting and preparing a future Industry-Initiated Partnership Project.The preparatory activities may cover the following aspects: The feasibility analysis for the intended system; The definition of the preliminary technical specifications and system baseline; The identification of technical, schedule, financial and other risks; The definition of all required strategic/business and financial elements that are necessary in support of the future Project Proposal; The definition of the organisation required to develop the system; Critical early stage pre-development of technology; Critical early stage validation of technology or service.

original.description: Under NAVISP Element 3, the Agency issues this Call for Proposals for the development of initiatives in the Position, Navigation and Timing domain. Element 3 is focused on participating States' priorities and aims at supporting their national navigation activities along the whole value chain. Element 3 configures as an ad-hoc support element, which is envisaged per country and possibly per domain, for the development and promotion of products, applications and services based on GNSS and more widely on PNT systems. Following participating states request, ESA may provide technical assistance in various areas. Element 3 configures as an opportunity for the participating States delegations to animate and coordinate discussions with national entities and to set up the processes to identify and federate institutional demands. This will foster cooperation as well as possible national partnerships with a wide diversity of actors, enlarging the national space community (agency, industries, universities, and research centres) and strengthening its relationships with authorities, organisations, institutions, industries, and research actors from non-space sectors. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 3 team to discuss the development of activities of national relevance and matching institutional interests. Details on the tendering process and preparing the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals.

original.description: The Luxembourg's National Programme - LuxIMPULSE Programme, aims to strengthen worldwide competitiveness of Luxembourg industry in the near term in existing markets and to establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of Luxembourg national priorities.The Call for Proposals is addressed only to economic operators - be it as Prime or Subcontractor level - registered in Luxembourg, unless otherwise instructed and approved by the Luxembourg Space Agency. The proposed work shall not overlap with any currently running ESA Contract awarded to any entity in the proposal consortium.Activities submitted in the frame of LuxIMPULSE Programme may be related to the study, improvement or development of space systems, subsystems, technology, ground systems for space applications, or downstream service products based on space data.It must be noted that according to the Procurement Regulations ESA/REG/001 rev. 5, Art. 18, Tenderers areeligible to participate in a tendering procedure of the Agency provided they possess the necessary professional and technical qualifications, professional and technical competences, financial resources, equipment and other physical facilities, managerial capability, reliability, experience and the personnel, to perform a Contract.The support to the activity by the Luxembourg Space Agency is mandatory. The activities selected will be funded by the Agency at a level depending on the nature of the economic operator and the maturity and proximity to market of the activity. The remainder will be funded by the economic operator's internal own resources and shall not include any additional source of public funding. The economic operator's contribution can be either monetary or in-kind.

original.description: This procurement targets the delivery of the Copernicus Space Component acquisition services, including the Sentinels X-Band data acquisition operations and the S-band Telemetry, Tracking and Control (TTC) services.The X-Band Acquisition service aims at the on-ground reception of data sensed by the Sentinel satellites and the delivery of the acquired data in the form of CADU data stream for further ground segment operations. The TTC services aim at the reception of the satellite telecommands, their modulation and radiation to the satellite.Although covering different functions of the Copernicus Space Component (CSC) operations, the above-mentioned services may be considered rather similar in terms of required infrastructure and operations capabilities of the service providers. Accordingly the current procurement will include the possibility to cover both services.Building upon the operational experience gathered in the past years since the launch of Sentinel-1A in 2014, ESA intends to procure as much as possible standardized services using Contractors' owned state-of-the-art, off-the-shelf facilities and satellite-independent interfaces.In order to maximize the competition and the value for money for the to-be-procured services, the Services will be procured through the ESA Framework Agreements procedure, as established at Article 15 of ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 3 which can be downloaded at the following URL http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). This procedure consists therefore in a two-step procurement approach, broken down as follows: Step 1 -Qualification Phase: The objective of this Step is to award, through an Open Competition Frame Contracts with the entities qualifying for the performance of the services subject of this procurement. Step 2 -Implementation Phase: The objective of this Step is to award, through Restricted Competitions between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step 1, the Work Orders allowing the performance of the procured services.An Information day about the subject procurement was organized at the European Space Agency (ESA) in December 2018. The location, date, registration process and Agenda of this briefing session was published on ESA Tendering website (EMITS) under "NEWS" (http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). Potential bidders are invited to consult regularly ESA Tendering website (EMITS).The Acquisition And TTC Services For Copernicus procurements will be fundedby the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators, which have their registered office in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway.In order to access the Frame ITT Package from EMITS, any economic operator interested in the subject procurement will have to be registered as a potential ESA Tenderer. To register with ESA as a potential Tenderer, you will be requestedto complete the online questionnaire available ESA-STAR registration website: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int. While the registration process is underway, potential ESA Tenderers may access the Frame ITT Package through ESA's dedicated Copernicus server, which is accessible at: https://copernicus-emits.esa.int/

original.description: This procurement targets the delivery of the Copernicus Space Component Long Term Archive service.The Long Term Archive service aims at the ingestion, archive, preservation and retrieval of Copernicus Sentinel products.In order to maximise the competition andvalue for money for the service to be procured, the Long Term Archive Service will be implemented through the ESA Framework Agreements procedure, as established at Article 15 of ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 3) which can be downloaded at the following URLhttp://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main).  This procedure consists of a two-step procurement approach, broken down as follows:Step 1 - Open Qualification Period: The objective of this Step is to award, through an Open Competition (Frame ITT), Frame Contracts to several  Frame-Contractors  (Competitive Frame Contracts)Step 2 - Long Term Archive Service Implementation: The objective of this Step is to award the Work Orders through Restricted Competitions (RFP) between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step 1, allowing the implementation of the requested Long Term Archive Service.An Information day for this procurement will be held at ESRIN at 10:00am CEST on July 12th 2019. Further information on this briefing session has been published on ESA Tendering website (EMITS) under NEWS (http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). Potential bidders are invited to consult regularly the ESA Tendering website. This Long Term Archive Service is funded by the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators, that have their registered office in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway. In order to access the Frame ITT Package from EMITS, any economic operator interested in the procurement will have to be registered as a potential ESA Tenderer. To register with ESA as a potential Tenderer, it is necessary to complete the online questionnaire available on the ESA-STAR registration website: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int. Whilst the registration process is underway, potential ESA Tenderers may access the Frame ITT Package through ESA's dedicated Copernicus server: https://copernicus-emits.esa.int/
